use: Putting papers, files, data or thoughts in order; for a messy room, katazukeru is more everyday.

example.romaji: ato de shorui seiri suru yo.
example.ja: 後で書類整理するよ。
example.english: I'll sort out the papers later.

examplePolite.romaji: ato de shorui o seiri shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 後で書類を整理します。
examplePolite.english: I'll sort out the papers later.

notes: Kimochi o seiri suru = sort out your feelings. Same sound as seiri, a period (menstruation).

example.ja: ここで靴脱いでね。
example.english: Take your shoes off here, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: koko de kutsu o nuide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ここで靴を脱いでください。
examplePolite.english: Please take your shoes off here.

notes: One verb takes everything off, but putting on splits: kiru (tops), haku (shoes, trousers), kaburu (hats).

use: Putting something into its proper place — a drawer, a cupboard, a bag.

example.ja: おもちゃ、ちゃんとしまってね。
example.english: Put your toys away properly, okay?

examplePolite.ja: おもちゃをちゃんとしまってください。
examplePolite.english: Please put your toys away properly.

notes: Also the ending -te shimau (-chau), 'end up doing': tabechatta = I ate it all.

use: Said of someone else's eating or drinking — a host to a guest, staff to a customer.

example.romaji: douzo, atsui uchi ni meshiagatte kudasai.
example.ja: どうぞ、熱いうちに召し上がってください。
example.english: Please, eat it while it's hot.

notes: Never for yourself: your own eating is itadaku or tabemasu.

english: decorate; put on display, put up
use: For pictures, flowers or decorations set out to be seen.

example.romaji: kono shashin, heya ni kazarou ka.
example.ja: この写真、部屋に飾ろうか。
example.english: Shall we put this photo up in the room?

examplePolite.romaji: kono shashin o heya ni kazarimashou ka.
examplePolite.ja: この写真を部屋に飾りましょうか。
examplePolite.english: Shall we put this photo up in the room?

notes: Kazaranai hito = a down-to-earth, unpretentious person.

english: tidy up; put away; clear (the table)
use: The everyday word for cleaning up a mess — a room, toys, dishes.

example.ja: お客さん来るから、部屋片付けて。
example.english: Guests are coming, so tidy your room.

examplePolite.romaji: okyakusan ga kuru node, heya o katazukete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: お客さんが来るので、部屋を片付けてください。
examplePolite.english: Guests are coming, so please tidy your room.

notes: Also for finishing off work: shigoto o katazukeru. Shimau is putting one thing in its place.

use: With a cloth or towel: tables, hands, tears, a wet body.

example.ja: ちょっとテーブル拭いてくれる?
example.english: Can you wipe the table?

examplePolite.romaji: chotto teeburu o fuite moraemasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: ちょっとテーブルを拭いてもらえますか?

notes: Same sound as fuku 'clothes' and fuku 'blow'.

use: Almost always shawaa o abiru; also sunlight or criticism pouring onto you.

example.romaji: saki ni shawaa abite kuru ne.
example.ja: 先にシャワー浴びてくるね。
example.english: I'll go take a shower first.

examplePolite.romaji: saki ni shawaa o abite kimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 先にシャワーを浴びてきます。
examplePolite.english: I'll go take a shower first.

notes: A bath is ofuro ni hairu, not abiru.

use: Above all ha o migaku, brushing your teeth; also shoes, or a skill (ude o migaku).

example.ja: 寝る前に歯磨いた?
example.english: Did you brush your teeth before bed?

examplePolite.romaji: neru mae ni ha o migakimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 寝る前に歯を磨きましたか?
examplePolite.english: Did you brush your teeth before bed?

notes: Hamigaki = brushing your teeth, or toothpaste.

english: put on, wear (shoes, socks, trousers, skirts)
use: For anything on the feet or legs; haite iru (haiteru) = be wearing.

example.ja: 今日はスカート履いていく。
example.english: I'm wearing a skirt today.

examplePolite.romaji: kyou wa sukaato o haite ikimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今日はスカートを履いていきます。

notes: Tops take kiru and hats kaburu. Same sound as haku 'throw up'.

use: Convenience store staff ask atatamemasu ka? about your bento.

example.ja: 昨日のカレー、温めようか?
example.english: Shall I heat up yesterday's curry?

examplePolite.romaji: kinou no karee o atatamemashou ka?
examplePolite.ja: 昨日のカレーを温めましょうか?
examplePolite.english: Shall I heat up yesterday's curry?

notes: Written 暖める for rooms and air; same sound.

english: hang out to dry; air (a futon)

example.ja: 洗濯物、外に干してくれた?
example.english: Did you hang the washing outside?

examplePolite.romaji: sentakumono o soto ni hoshite kuremashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 洗濯物を外に干してくれましたか?
examplePolite.english: Did you hang the washing outside?

notes: Bringing it back in is toriireru. Futon o hosu = air the futon in the sun.

example.ja: 乾いたら洗濯物畳んでおいてね。
example.english: Fold the laundry once it's dry, okay?

examplePolite.romaji: kawaitara sentakumono o tatande oite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 乾いたら洗濯物を畳んでおいてください。
examplePolite.english: Please fold the laundry once it's dry.

notes: Also mise o tatamu = close a shop for good.

use: A daytime nap, often after lunch.

example.romaji: gohan no ato, chotto hirune suru.
example.ja: ご飯の後、ちょっと昼寝する。
example.english: I'm going to take a quick nap after lunch.

examplePolite.romaji: gohan no ato, sukoshi hirune shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ご飯の後、少し昼寝します。
examplePolite.english: I'm going to take a short nap after lunch.

notes: Also a noun: hirune no jikan = nap time.

use: The classic excuse for being late.

example.ja: ごめん、今朝寝坊しちゃった!
example.english: Sorry, I overslept this morning!

examplePolite.ja: すみません、今朝寝坊しました。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry, I overslept this morning.

example.romaji: yasai to niku, issho ni itameru dake da yo.
example.ja: 野菜と肉、一緒に炒めるだけだよ。
example.english: You just stir-fry the veg and meat together.

examplePolite.romaji: yasai to niku o issho ni itameru dake desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 野菜と肉を一緒に炒めるだけですよ。
examplePolite.english: You just stir-fry the vegetables and meat together.

notes: Itamemono = a stir-fry. Deep-frying is ageru.

example.romaji: ashita hayaoki shinakya ikenai n da.
example.ja: 明日早起きしなきゃいけないんだ。
example.english: I have to get up early tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita wa hayaoki shinai to ikenai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日は早起きしないといけないんです。
examplePolite.english: I have to get up early tomorrow.

notes: Also a noun for the habit: hayaoki da ne = you're an early riser.

example.ja: お茶入れるから、お湯沸かして。
example.english: I'll make tea, so boil some water.

examplePolite.romaji: ocha o ireru node, oyu o wakashite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: お茶を入れるので、お湯を沸かしてください。
examplePolite.english: I'll make tea, so please boil some water.

notes: Ofuro o wakasu = heat the bath. Water boiling by itself is waku: oyu ga waita.

use: From the microwave's ding; the everyday word at home.

example.ja: これ、3分ぐらいチンして。
example.english: Microwave this for about three minutes.

examplePolite.romaji: kore o sanpun gurai chin shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: これを3分ぐらいチンしてください。
examplePolite.english: Please microwave this for about three minutes.

notes: The neutral way to say it is renji de atatameru.

example.ja: 昨日また夜更かししちゃったよ。
example.english: I stayed up late again last night.

examplePolite.ja: 昨日また夜更かししてしまいました。
examplePolite.english: I stayed up late again last night.

notes: The opposite habit is hayaoki, getting up early.
